result:
I'll set this up as a new project rather than run a gap analysis. Nothing is built yet: the package is a greeting `main()` with two smoke tests. The prompt and the three research files are background, so every outcome below is a **candidate** taken from your brief (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`). Please confirm or strike each one.

The brief's Parts A and B (literature review, gap table, data inventory) are already covered by the three research files. I've left them out as outcomes, so the list below is what the code delivers.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked, all from `ces-revisions-prompt.md`)

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | A tidy panel of CES estimates by release: total nonfarm and supersectors, SA and NSA, each print plus preliminary and final benchmarks, across all four revision steps | Data is small: roughly 550 months × ~12 series × 2 (SA/NSA) × ~5 vintages ≈ 66k values, a few MB. Your time to reconcile archived releases is the real cost, and I can't estimate it until we see how far machine-readable vintages go back. |
| O2 | Descriptive revision scale over time for each revision step (MAR and dispersion, tails, the 2003 and 2020–22 breaks) | Negligible compute once O1 exists |
| O3 | A collection-interval covariate (days from reference week to first closing and release) plus first-, second- and third-closing collection rates | Days come from the calendar, so they're free. The earliest year of published collection rates is unknown to me. |
| O4 | Hand-built capacity covariates: real BLS appropriations, FTE, CES sample size, and shutdown, CR and sequestration indicators | About 40 fiscal years × 3–4 figures ≈ 120–160 hand-entered numbers from budget justifications and FedScope. Mostly your time. |
| O5 | Estimates of how collection interval moves the **scale** of the one-month (and two-month) revision | Fit time unknown; only running it can tell |
| O6 | A decomposition of SA revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, via joint NSA/SA vintages | Fit time unknown |
| O7 | Benchmark error as an irregular, higher-precision observation with wedge-back, giving benchmark-revision scale by supersector (birth–death heterogeneity) | Fit time unknown; ~11 supersectors × ~40 benchmarks |
| O8 | Whatever capacity effects (O4) on revision scale are actually identified, with horseshoe shrinkage and party shown only as a descriptive grouping | Fit time unknown; identification is expected to be weak |
| O9 | One unified multi-vintage model (latent path, SV plus covariates on log-scale, Student-t, supersector pooling) with PPC, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, and pseudo-real-time checks | Probably the dominant compute cost; only running it can tell |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: source manifests for archived releases, traceability of hand-built covariates, full validation suites.

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Vintage data and description (known progression): O1, O2.** Every other track reads this panel.
- **B — Collection interval (research): O3, O5.** Split from C–E because the within-year calendar answer stands without any capacity covariate.
- **C — Seasonal vs sample (research): O6.** Split out because the decomposition answers a measurement question unrelated to the drivers.
- **D — Benchmark and wedge-back (research): O7.** Split out because it concerns a different revision step and a different error source (birth–death and QCEW realignment).
- **E — Operational capacity (research): O4, O8.** Split out because its collinear, trending covariates shouldn't hold up B–D's answers.
- **F — Unified model (research): O9.** This combines B–E. You may prefer to fold it into one of them.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv, pytest and ruff (from the repo).
- NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax only if warranted, ArviZ and Polars (from your brief).
- National CES only, in thousands of jobs (from your brief).

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions` → `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. That file doesn't exist yet.

**Optional probes** (I'll run them only if you say yes):
1. Download BLS's CES vintage archive once, to firm up O1's earliest vintage date and format.
2. Install `jax` and `numpyro` under Python 3.14, to confirm wheels exist before anything depends on them.

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds, and the name, and say yes or no to the probes.
